Spain’s prime minister Pedro Sánchez said on Friday that he was convinced he would ⁠secure a left-wing majority ⁠in a snap ​general election despite adverse public polling, as the political parties prepared to wrap up campaigning ahead of Sunday’s vote, Reuters reported.
Amid a legal ban on publishing new ⁠opinion surveys, the Socialist leader insisted that internal data suggested his party would win the most votes, allowing him to clinch re-election with the support of smaller ⁠leftist allies.
“I can’t conceive of us losing,” Sanchez told radio station SER, adding that left-leaning voters were ​increasingly mobilising to turn out in droves, a ‌prerequisite for reaching a progressive ‌majority to tackle issues such as the country’s deep housing crisis.
double quotation mark “When progressive Spain gets going, it’s unstoppable.”
However, nearly all the polls released before ‌the ban showed a clear advantage for a potential coalition between the conservative People’s Party and far-right Vox, which seek to oust Sanchez after eight years in power.
Freelance journalist based in Madrid and host of the Sobremesa podcast
Vox has often been portrayed in international coverage as a party of Franco nostalgists whose ultraconservative Catholicism and civil-war rhetoric towards the separatist Catalan “enemy within” threatened a return to the worst of Spain’s recent past.
Yet since its disappointing showing at the 2023 general election, Abascal has purged much of the party’s original leadership and overseen an ideological renewal.
In looking to update its messaging, Vox has blended elements of Marine Le Pen’s welfare chauvinism , such as the concept of “national priority”, with ideas coming from the pan-European, white nationalist identitarian movement.
Virtually absent from Spanish political debate a year ago, national priority would give Spaniards preferential access to social housing, public services and welfare benefits, with Vox already securing PP backing for the principle in regional coalition deals.
In September, however, the European Commission warned that even the residence-based criteria used at a regional level could discriminate against citizens of other EU member states. Vox’s general election manifesto goes further, pledging to exclude all non-Spanish citizens from the country’s minimum-income benefit.
If the polls are right, PP’s Alberto Núñez Feijóo could become prime minister on a lower vote share than the PP secured in the last election. He would then owe his majority to Vox’s surge and support in coalition, and Abascal would have both the leverage and the incentive to show his voters what the party can deliver in office.
A coalition formed on those terms could also foreshadow a closer alliance between conservatives and the far right at a European level. A Le Pen victory in the French presidential election next spring would put the nationalist right at the head of one of the EU’s two most influential states, shifting the political centre of gravity in Brussels and opening the way for a durable governing bloc to the right of the EU’s traditional grand coalition.
It was not by chance that Vox opened its election campaign with a rally displaying video messages of support from Le Pen, Meloni and AfD’s Alice Weidel. Having drawn on its far-right European allies to reinvent itself, Vox could now in turn strengthen their hand if it is successful in becoming the PP’s kingmaker after Sunday’s vote.
Sánchez’s defeat would also deprive the centre left of its strongest counterweight in the European Council, where he is the only social democrat to represent one of the EU’s major powers.
Speaking to the Vox rally, Weidel proclaimed: “All of Europe is waiting for a political change in Madrid.” All of Europe may not be waiting for such a change, but it is certainly watching.
Sitting on a park bench, taking in the sunny day, Naima reflected on all that had seemingly changed since she moved to Spain three decades earlier.
Back then, the Moroccan national had felt warmly welcomed by Spaniards. “I had never, at any point in my life, felt like there was racism,” she said.
“But now things are changing. And the blame lies with rightwing politics.”
Over the years, she has steadily watched as a growing crop of politicians sought to win votes by demonising migrants, minorities and Muslims. The impact reverberated deeply in places such as Torre-Pacheco, whose fertile fields and constant demand for farmhands has long attracted workers from around the world.
“They peddle racism, and lots of people end up suffering,” said Naima, 53. “Here everyone knows me, but others speak of being treated differently, looked at in a certain way, or having gestures made at them.”
On Sunday, Spain is set to gain a glimpse of how deeply engrained these divisions have become as voters cast their ballots in a snap general election.
Most polls suggest the government of the Socialist leader, Pedro Sánchez, will be replaced by a rightwing coalition led by the conservative People’s party (PP) and supported by the far-right, anti-immigration Vox party.
If so, it will be the first time that a far-right party has governed Spain since the return to democracy after the death of General Franco.
No new polls are allowed to be published in Spain in the five days before a Spanish election, but one company has found a surprising solución alternativa.
The Adelaide Review ran from 1984 to 2020, covering the city’s cultural and artistic life until Covid and upheavals in the media world made it “untenable”, its editor, Amanda Pepe , wrote in the final edition .
But now it has found unexpected new life as an, erm, back passage for Spanish polls in the blackout period.
The Review site is now owned by a company called Prensa Ibérica, which also runs the Spanish newspaper El Periódico.
An article on the Periódico website that links to the poll criticises “outdated legislation” that lets political parties see polls, but not citizens.
“The Adelaide Review’s daily poll addresses this issue, giving citizens access to the same information used by politicians,” it said.
It’s probably a good moment to say that we will be running a special Europe live blog from Madrid on Sunday night to bring you all the latest in the Spanish parliamentary election, including first polls, projections, reactions, and analysis.
Last night’s debate between the leaders of Spain’s four biggest political parties was a rambling, ratty and revealing spectacle in which Ada Colau, the leader of the leftwing Broad Front, is generally agreed to have come out on top.
Colau, a former Barcelona mayor, was committed and forensic in her attacks on Vox’s leader, Santiago Abascal, over his refusal to condemn gender-based violence.
She and the socialist leader and current prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, also joined forces to question the economic wisdom of the far-right party’s plans for €112bn of public spending costs, and to defend the benefits of immigration.
Sánchez – who was far more animated and engaged in this debate than in last week’s head-to-head with Alberto Núñez Feijóo, the leader of Spain’s conservative People’s party (PP) – was happy to wind up his rival over his lack of English skills.
Before Feijóo could answer a question from Colau about the PP’s proposed tax cuts, Sánchez – a fluent English speaker – quipped:
“I’m sorry to say that Mr Feijóo’s maths are about as good as his English.”
Vox’s Abascal was keen to keep the focus on immigration and on corruption – a problem, he added, “that ruins and kills”.
Feijóo also sought to attack Sánchez’s government over corruption , the two deadly rail crashes suffered this year, and over the summer’s mass border crossing into the North African territory of Ceuta.
He argued that his 30-year political career was unblemished by corruption allegations while suggesting that Sánchez was a “corruption magnet”. That led the prime minister to bring up the infamous mid-1990s holiday photos that show Feijóo hangin…

Watch: Zelensky questions "strange" Trump-Putin friendship in BBC interview
Volodymyr Zelensky has voiced deep frustration with the US, criticising Donald Trump for calling Vladimir Putin "my friend" and saying delays in delivering vital anti-ballistic missiles were costing Ukrainian lives.
In an interview with the BBC at his central Kyiv office, Ukraine's president complained the US was not pushing Russia hard enough in peace talks, and called it "strange" that Trump posted a photo of himself embracing Putin.
"Of course it's up to the President of the United States, but... it's strange," Zelensky said, speaking in English.
"He's an aggressor, and a killer…He can't be a friend. Just cannot be," he said, adding it was like saying you were friends with Adolf Hitler during World War Two.
Since a bruising encounter with Trump in the Oval Office in 2025, Zelensky has been careful how he handles relations with the United States.
Trump's two envoys have been trying to negotiate a peace deal between Russia and Ukraine - to end the huge loss of life. But they often seem more in tune with Moscow's position, than that of Kyiv.
The latest round of peace talks, mediated in Abu Dhabi earlier this month, made no obvious progress: "The more we know, the more problems", is how Zelensky described it.
On Thursday, Donald Trump posted on his Truth Social platform that at his own summit with Putin in China last week he had urged Russia to "pull back all military aggression against territories throughout Europe" and said he believed a peace deal with Ukraine was "a strong possibility".
But from its public statements, Russia appears to have regressed to its initial, hardline negotiating positions – on everything.
And Zelensky revealed that it was not clear whether European negotiators would be at the table, as the US envoys had announced .
Europe ready for talks with Russia on ending war in Ukraine, leaders say
Zelensky says Putin is a 'killer' after Trump calls Russian leader a friend
Ukraine urgently needs the talks to move forward and bring five exhausting years of Russia's full-scale invasion to an end.
Russian strikes across the country have been growing more frequent and more deadly: the number of civilians being killed is at an all-time high.
So Zelensky called for "real helpful allies, who can push Russia" to achieve results and urged the US to live up to its reputation as a strong country with "power and respect".
"When you try to be very neutral with the aggressor... it means you support victims and you support also aggressor. It's not right," he said.
The US argues that it is neutral: in the complex search for a peace deal between the two sides that can hold.
Questioned again on Thursday about calling Putin a friend, Trump told reporters: "We want to stop killing. I could say he's not a friend... I want to make a deal."
He added: "I could walk in and say, I don't like you, and then we have the same problem that we have with Zelensky and Putin.
"You know... the biggest problem to that settlement is the fact that you have two leaders that really hate each other."
The air alerts, day and night, are now a draining feature of everyday life. As Russian ballistic missiles target power stations and bridges, jet-powered drones are launched daily at central Kyiv and other big cities.
Ukraine launches hundreds of drones at targets in Russia in response.
Zelensky said the military here are now able to destroy about 70% of Russia's fastest drones, a statistic he said was improving.
But there is a "very, very big" deficit of interceptors to stop ballistic missiles and he said the Americans were delaying deliveries of its Patriot systems.
"It's a pity they made a focus on Middle East and they help them more… It's a pity. We have huge questions with this," Zelensky said.
He also confirmed that the US satellite communications system, Starlink – and its military version, Starshield – were still being restricted in occupied areas of Ukraine.
Ukrainian drone units have described their problems to the BBC, as their interceptor drones can no longer catch up with Russian Shaheds. It means those weapons then fly deeper into Ukraine, unhindered.
"Technically SpaceX, politically - I don't know, I really don't know," Zelensky replied. "It's like... ping pong. We are asking one side, they say it's the other."
Ukraine's own long-range strikes against Russian targets have increased in recent weeks, including oil refineries and ships carrying weapons or fuel.
On Thursday, Italy's Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said an attack that sank a Russian warship docked in eastern Libya this week risked spreading war to the Mediterranean, which was unacceptable.
Zelensky defended the move, calling the warship Merkury an "absolutely fair goal".
He accepted that such strikes were "very dangerous" but said Ukraine's forces "never attack" without co-ordinating with its partners.
But he acknowledged that Ukraine was bracing for a difficult and dangerous winter.
Recent attacks on Kyiv have targeted bridges over the vast river Dnipro, apparently trying to cut the city in two.
Some residents have already left town for the winter and businesses closed, as power cuts and strikes on logistics networks have pushed operating costs unmanageably high.
"People can go, but we will try to defend our capital in any way. We need our capital. Without a capital, you don't have a country."

Patterson, 52, seeks leave to appeal to Australia’s highest court over deaths of estranged family members after fatal beef wellington lunch
Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast
Erin Patterson has applied to the high court seeking leave to appeal after a failed bid last month to overturn her triple murder conviction.
Patterson, 52, was found guilty last year of the murders of her estranged husband’s parents, Don and Gail Patterson, and his aunt Heather Wilkinson, after she hosted them for lunch.
She was also convicted of the attempted murder of Heather’s husband, Ian Wilkinson, who survived eating beef wellington laced with death cap mushrooms after spending weeks in hospital.
On Friday afternoon, her lawyers filed her application to try to overturn her convictions and life sentence in the high court, a source confirmed to Guardian Australia.
Victoria’s court of appeal last month ruled Patterson’s appeal against her convictions should be dismissed . But it granted an appeal by the director of public prosecutions against Patterson’s sentence, finding that her original sentence of life imprisonment with a non-parole period of 33 years was too lenient. She was resentenced to life without parole.
“This offending was extraordinarily cold and calculated and stands to be denounced in the strongest terms,” court of appeal justices Lesley Taylor, Stephen McLeish and Peter Kidd found in their judgment on 30 October.
“Necessarily, we have given the question whether it is inappropriate to fix a non-parole period anxious consideration, in light of the gravity of such a conclusion and the different view to which the experienced sentencing judge came.
“But the features of the offending … lead each of us to conclude that this is a case of such shocking criminality that it is inappropriate to fix a non-parole period.”
Patterson had 28 days from that judgment to apply for special leave to appeal to the high court , a period that ended on Friday.
Her written application for leave to appeal is expected to be determined by all seven high court justices.
If they cannot make a determination based on the written application, the justices can refer the application to a hearing for oral argument.
Applications are typically referred to the justices the week before a sitting period and considered that Monday, before decisions are published the following Thursday.
The high court’s last sitting period of the year runs from 30 November to 11 December, meaning Patterson could know the fate of her application within the next fortnight.
If not, the court does not sit again until 1 February. The court would not comment on the application.
Patterson’s lawyers had previously argued in the court of appeal that her convictions should be overturned on seven grounds, all but two of which were dismissed without leave to appeal granted.
The two grounds for which Patterson was granted leave to appeal, but were also dismissed, related to the sequestration of the jury during their deliberations, and the telephone cell tower and iNaturalist evidence presented during her trial.
The court heard that the jury in the case stayed at the same motel as the police informant and DPP staff while they were deciding on their verdicts in the trial.
Patterson argued that this represented “a fundamental irregularity … that has fatally undermined the integrity of the verdicts and requires the quashing of the convictions and an order for a re-trial so that justice can not only be done but be seen to be done”.
The second ground was that cell tower evidence, which suggested Patterson could have been in Loch and Outtrim after death cap mushroom sightings were reported in the towns on the citizen science website iNaturalist, should not have been adduced in her trial as it was either irrelevant, or its relevance was “outweighed by its unfair prejudice”.

Patterson was last year found guilty of murdering three relatives
Australia's mushroom killer Erin Patterson has launched a final legal bid to overturn her murder convictions and avoid dying in jail.
Erin Patterson, 52, was last year found guilty of murdering three relatives and attempting to kill another when she served them a toxic mushroom-laced meal in 2023.
Last month, in Victoria's Court of Appeal three judges dismissed an appeal against her convictions and threw out the possibility she could be released on parole – saying her crimes were "extraordinarily cold and calculated" and had to be "denounced in the strongest terms".
She has now made a last-ditch application to the High Court to look at her case.
Patterson had 28 days to file an application for special leave to appeal to the High Court, a deadline which expired on Friday.
She wants the country's top judges to examine both her conviction and sentence - but the court does not have to agree to look at the case. It only hears appeals in about 10% of cases.
After a high-profile trial last year, a jury found Patterson guilty of murdering her in-laws, Don and Gail Patterson, and Gail's sister Heather Wilkinson, by serving them individual portions of beef Wellington containing death cap mushrooms which she had tracked down, foraged and prepared.
Patterson was also found guilty of the attempted murder of Heather's husband Ian Wilkinson, a local pastor, who also ate the toxic lunch at Patterson's home in rural Victoria.
He survived after spending weeks in hospital and has ongoing health issues due to the poisoning.
Simon Patterson, the host's estranged husband, was meant to attend the lunch but cancelled at the last minute, in part due to his belief that his wife had repeatedly tried to poison him over several years.
Patterson was sentenced last September, with the trial judge allowing a non-parole period of 33 years due to the "harsh prison conditions" she would likely face. This glimmer of hope of freedom was thrown out by the appeal judges, who ruled she should never be released.
She had argued her conviction was unsafe on seven grounds - including a hotel booking mix up which saw the jury stay in the same place as the prosecution, a key police witness and the media.
Her lawyers said this was "catastrophic" and undermined the integrity of her trial, but the appeal court judges dismissed all the grounds for appeal.

Taiwanese officials raise alarm over interference by China in elections that will shape fortunes of ruling party
Taiwanese voters go to the polls on Saturday in closely watched local elections that will shape the fortunes of the ruling Democratic Progressive party (DPP) as it navigates an increasingly precarious set of relationships on the global stage.
Saturday’s vote will choose mayors, council members and other local leaders across 22 districts. Unlike the presidential elections, in which foreign policy is often a key issue, the local elections, held every four years , are largely focused on bread-and-butter issues such as housing affordability and wealth distribution.
Nevertheless, China looms large over the vote, which takes place against the background of intense military pressure from Beijing . China claims Taiwan as part of its territory despite never having ruled the self-governing island. Taiwanese officials have raised the alarm over thousands of incidents of suspected misinformation or election interference, and certain candidates have been subjected to harassment from the Chinese authorities. There have also been reports of hundreds of China-linked AI-generated videos spreading disinformation about Taiwanese politicians disliked by Beijing.
Beijing calls the allegations of election interference “completely fabricated”. Zhu Fenglian, a spokesperson for China’s Taiwan affairs office, said the allegations “stir up anti-China sentiment to win votes”.
Wei-Ting Yen, a political scientist at Academia Sinica, Taiwan’s national research academy, said: “Even though local elections are not about China, the outcome of local elections will have huge implications for cross-strait relations.”
Most races are a tight competition between a candidate from the ruling DPP and the main opposition party, the Kuomintang (KMT). The KMT promotes closer ties with Beijing, and its chair, Cheng Li-wun, travelled to China this year to meet Xi Jinping, China’s leader. Xi has vowed to unify China with Taiwan, and has not ruled out using military action to achieve that aim.
Yen said if the KMT loses some of its traditional strongholds, Beijing “may need to reconsider what is the most effective strategy for influencing Taiwanese people”.
One of the most contentious votes is the race for Taipei mayor, an office that the DPP has not held for nearly three decades. The DPP has selected as its challenger Puma Shen, a national legislator whom Beijing declared a “diehard separatist” in 2024. It is the first time a candidate under sanctions by Beijing has run to be mayor of Taiwan’s capital city. In the neighbouring New Tapei City race, the DPP’s Su Chiao-hui is also proving to be a ferocious challenger to the incumbent KMT.
Shen said in a recent interview that even if he didn’t win, the capital’s mayoral race was “a slap to China” because it proved that “democracy works here in Taiwan”.
Huang Bo-kai, a 23-year-old law student, said his top concern was cross-strait relations and how US-China relations were evolving. “The world’s three major powers are increasingly willing to flex their muscles: the US attacking Iran, Russia attacking Ukraine. I think Taiwan could very well be the next target [of China],” he told the Guardian.
Taiwan’s president, the DPP’s Lai Ching-te, is detested by Beijing and has taken a bolshier stance on cross-strait relations than his predecessor, Tsai Ing-wen, who was admired for her ability to drum up support in Washington while walking a delicate tightrope to avoid angering China.
Lai has pushed for greater spending on weapons to deter military aggression from China. The government has proposed a record 18% increase in defence spending for next year, including for drones and missiles, taking it above 1tn Taiwan dollars (£23bn) for the first time.
But many Taiwanese voters would rather that money was spent on more immediate economic issues. Lev Nachman, a political scientist at National Taiwan University, said the national leaders of the DPP and KMT had been notably absent from the mayoral races, reflecting the extent to which campaigns were focused on local issues.
Going into the campaigns for the 2028 presidential elections, Lai would “try to take advantage of the momentum that [Shen] and Su have built for the DPP,” Nachman said, noting that support for those candidates would not necessarily translate into support for Lai.
Tony Yeh, a Taipei man in his 70s, said: “To put it simply, the authorities should do more to boost the economy and buy fewer weapons.”
Taiwan’s economy has boomed this year, largely thanks to the pivotal role that its semiconductor industry plays in the global artificial intelligence rally. The economy grew by more than 14% in the first nine months of the year, the fastest rate in 50 years. But nearly 70% of workers earned less than the average monthly wage of 49,152 Taiwan dollars (£1,137) in the same period.
Yeh said: “Most traditional industries are having a really tough time.”
William Yang, a senior analyst at the International Crisis Group, said: “The issues that really are going to determine their votes are livelihood issues including the stagnant wage, the astronomically high housing price, the affordability issue, and how the government can better make sure Taiwan’s incredible economic boom fuelled by the global AI growth is going to be distributed more evenly.”
Other voters have more niche concerns. Walking her dog in a park, Kuo Wei-tong, a nail salon worker, said policies affecting pets were among her top concerns.
“People are having fewer children and getting more cats and dogs,” she said. “I think that’s something worth giving serious consideration to as well.”

Dropping of corruption charges against Israeli PM after unusual intervention could set damaging precedent
The Israeli judges presiding over Benjamin Netanyahu’s corruption trial have called on prosecutors to end proceedings, a highly unusual intervention that leaves the attorney general facing a momentous political decision.
The prime minister has been charged with bribery, fraud and breach of trust in three complex and overlapping criminal cases that hinge on his relationship with telecoms magnates and other wealthy businessmen. Ending the trial without a ruling could set damaging precedents for media independence and how politicians are held to account.
“There were evidentiary difficulties in the case, but the position the judges laid out effectively means abandoning the media to the whims of politicians and publishers, and setting an impossible bar for conviction in corruption cases,” said Yael Freidson, the legal correspondent for Haaretz, who has covered the trial since it began in 2020.
The judges urged prosecutors to drop one case because “the chances of a conviction are low”, seek a plea deal in a second, and reconsider the third set of charges. Even if prosecutors were to prove the allegations of fraud and breach of trust in that case, it was not clear that Netanyahu’s alleged behaviour amounted to criminal conduct, they said.
The attorney general, Gali Baharav-Miara, who was summoned to court to hear the judges’ statement in person, must now decide whether to accept their recommendations and end a trial that has dominated and shaped Israeli politics for the best part of a decade.
The decision is not straightforward, even though the current bench has in effect indicated a not guilty verdict is a foregone conclusion. If the trial continues, their ruling could still be appealed to a higher court, where fresh judges could take a different stance.
“[The former prime minister] Ehud Olmert was acquitted on all charges by the district court and was subsequently convicted by the supreme court on a minor charge,” Ben Caspit wrote in Maariv. “It ain’t over till it’s over.”
“[Baharav-Miara] could opt to reach a lenient plea bargain agreement with the defendant and put it all to rest, but that would be an admission of the entire justice system’s failure and would further fuel the conspiracy theories that Netanyahu and his disciples have been pumping ever since he was indicted.”
Settling or dropping all charges would immediately and permanently absolve Netanyahu, ending the threat of jail time and dispelling the legal shadow hanging over his political future.
A bill making its way through the opposition-controlled parliament would in effect bar him from serving as prime minister until the trial was concluded.
Netanyahu, who has pleaded not guilty to all charges, claims he is the victim of a political witch-hunt and welcomed the judges’ recommendation as a vindication. “The truth has finally come to light,” he said.
Baharav-Miara has withstood pressure from the judges in the case twice before. In 2023 and in 2025 they urged prosecutors to drop bribery charges, the most serious ones that Netanyahu faces, although they stopped short of suggesting the whole trial should be wrapped up.
Perhaps the single point of agreement between Netanyahu’s supporters and his critics in relation to the trial is concern that it has been allowed to drag on for too long. Testimony from Netanyahu had extended over a year and a half, across 98 hearings, the longest by a single witness in Israeli judicial history, Freidson said. The transcripts from all the hearings run to more than 60,000 pages.
Oren Persico has sat in every hearing since the case began in 2020, covering it for the investigative magazine The Seventh Eye. Over that period he watched the judges slowly lose control of their courtroom, he said.
“It started with giving the defence a lot of rope to do what they wanted. Netanyahu’s lawyer lashed out at the prosecution and humiliated them, almost every day, and attacked the judges, which should be an absolute red line in court,” he said. “I think the judges are afraid and tired; they just want to get it all over with.”
The sense of a bench cracking under pressure was exacerbated by the recommendation to reconsider charges in one of the cases against Netanyahu. These were laid out by prosecutors seven years ago, and have not changed since, prompting joking questions about whether the judges had even read the indictment, and serious ones about their political judgment.
When Netanyahu was indicted, he decided to fight the charges both inside and outside the courtroom, declaring war on the prosecution, the media, the police and key democratic and judicial institutions, Persico said.
“To keep himself out of jail, he tried to form an authoritarian state here in Israel, which tore apart society. I understand the interest in putting an end to that,” Persico said. “But ending the trial would send a terrible message to criminals and politicians and media bosses: that if you fight strongly enough you can get away with anything.”

Iran has openly claimed its strikes on Gulf states throughout the war. So why is it denying an attack on Kuwait?
Two Italian technicians have been killed in a drone attack on a military site in Kuwait on Thursday, the first European civilians to die amid the United States-Israel war on Iran.
Kuwait and Italy have both blamed Iran. Tehran, which has for the most part not denied, outright, strikes on US military assets hosted by its Gulf neighbours and described those attacks as self-defence, has this time denied any role and has suggested the strike was a “false-flag” operation.
The denial has raised two questions: Who was behind the attack and, if it was Iran, why is it not taking responsibility?
On Thursday, several drones targeted military installations in Kuwait, according to Italy’s Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani.
Kuwait’s army initially described the target only as a “vital site”. Tajani later told the Italian Senate that it included an air-defence detection station where two technicians from Rheinmetall Italia, the Italian arm of the German defence company, were working.
The men were named by Italian media as Antonio Saccoccio, 65, from Formia, and Emanuele Lo Russo, 36, from Rome. They were maintaining detection antennae for the Skyguard air defence system used by Kuwait’s armed forces.
They were killed by falling shrapnel after the drones were intercepted, according to Kuwaiti and Italian reports. A Kuwaiti and a Pakistani national were injured.
The two dead men are the first European civilians to be killed as a result of the US-Israel war on Iran since it began in late February. A French soldier was killed in a drone attack in Iraq in March.
This was the first fatal strike on Kuwait in several months, although the country has been one of the hardest-hit Gulf states during the war. Its oil facilities, power infrastructure and airport have all been targeted at various points in the conflict. An Indian traveller was killed and 63 people were injured when drones hit Kuwait international airport on June 3 .
Both countries have blamed Iran for Thursday’s drone strike.
Kuwait’s Foreign Ministry condemned what it called a “sinful” attack and said the country reserved its right to take all measures to protect its sovereignty and the security of its citizens and residents.
After a call between Kuwait’s foreign minister and Tajani, the Kuwaiti ministry said the two had jointly condemned the strike.
Tajani told the Italian parliament the drones were “of Iranian origin”. The Gulf Cooperation Council’s secretary-general, Jasem Albudaiwi, also condemned what he called a “brutal attack”.
“The incident is suspicious and looks like a pre-cooked recipe for war,” Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi wrote on X.
Araghchi called both his Kuwaiti and Italian counterparts to deny Iranian involvement and offered to mount a joint investigation, according to Iran’s foreign ministry. As of Thursday evening, Kuwait had not publicly commented on the call with Araghchi.
Armed forces spokesman Abolfazl Shekarchi, speaking for both the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and the regular army, said Iranian forces had conducted “no military or offensive operations whatsoever” in the region. He called the attack a “false flag” operation, while a military statement accused the US and Israel of using it as cover for continued aggression.
The Iranian embassy in Rome said it “categorically rejects the allegation”, suggesting the attack could have been staged to drag Europe into the Iran war.
The denial stands out because Iran has rarely disowned its attacks since US-Israeli strikes began in February. In November alone, it issued five statements claiming strikes on neighbouring states, four of them on Bahrain and Kuwait.
Tehran usually tries to justify those strikes as self-defence, arguing that it targets US bases from which Iran is attacked, not the countries that host them.
This is not the first time Iran has denied an attack on Kuwait, however. When a power and desalination plant was hit on March 30 , killing an Indian worker, Iran also claimed that Israel was responsible.
Hassan Ahmadian, a professor of Middle East studies at the University of Tehran, said Iran’s record of claiming its strikes should be taken seriously.
“Whenever the Iranians do something, they announce it,” he told Al Jazeera. “This time, as on three or four occasions during the war, they said, ‘This wasn’t us.'”
He argued that Iran would have little reason to hide this attack. “They’ve struck the Americans,” he said. “Would they be afraid to announce they’d hit Italians?”
Ahmadian said other parties in the region, such as Israel, might want to “complicate the situation” by blaming Iran, which he called “the ready-made party to blame”. He added that some in Iran also suspect Ukraine, which he argued has been trying to raise its strategic value to Washington.
As the US ran down its stock of expensive Patriot missile interceptor systems against a barrage of cheap, mass-produced Iranian Shahed drones, Ukraine offered its expertise to the US in March on how to combat the drones, which are also used by Russia.
Ahmadian said US involvement could not be ruled out either. Iran has previously told regional governments that the US was behind strikes on two sites during the war, he said.
“We’re looking at someone fishing in troubled waters. Otherwise, if it were the Iranians, they would have announced it,” he added.
Paolo von Schirach, president of the Global Policy Institute and a professor of political science at Bay Atlantic University in Washington, dismissed the idea of US involvement.
“It’s bizarre to suggest the United States would coordinate this attack on Kuwait, an ally in the Gulf, just to stir up feelings,” he said.
Von Schirach noted that Italy has refused to join the US war on Iran and does not support it. “Italy isn’t on America’s side in this conflict,” he said. “So we shouldn’t take this seriously.”
Muhanad Seloom, a senior non-resident fellow at the Middle East Council on Global Affairs, said it was important to “separate Iranian-made from Iranian-launched and Iranian-ordered”.
Tajani described the drone as Iranian-built, of a type also used by Iran-backed militias. Seloom said that makes an Iraqi armed faction the leading alternative suspect. Such groups have claimed attacks on US forces in Gulf states since the war began.
He called Yemen’s Houthis “a distant second” and said Tehran’s own suspects, the US, Israel and Ukraine, “come with no evidence”.
“Only debris, radar tracks and a launch point can settle it,” he told Al Jazeera.
Seloom said Tehran first used it in March over strikes on Turkiye, Cyprus and Azerbaijan . However, he said that The Soufan Center, a US-based security think tank, found that it failed to convince Baku.
Claims have run the other way, too. The best known was the reported arrest of Mossad agents plotting bombings in Qatar and Saudi Arabia, which came to nothing, Seloom said, because neither of those governments stood behind it.
“Alleged often, verified never, as far as I can establish,” he said. “What this war has is deniable action. Hiding the author is common. Framing someone else has yet to be shown.”
In the case of Thursday’s attack, he said, Iran’s false-flag claim “stands without evidence so far”.
Abdullah al-Shayji, a professor of political science at Kuwait University, said Iran’s narrative “doesn’t come close to being rational or acceptable”.
“Iran bombed us eight days ago, on the 18th of this month, and didn’t deny it,” he said. He said Iran had fired 925 missiles and drones at Kuwait since the start of the war, and more projectiles at Gulf states and Jordan than at Israel. “This doesn’t fool anyone,” he said.
Al-Shayji said the denial comes down to who was killed and where. “Italian technicians were killed, and not at a US base,” he said.

Konser, saat 20.30’da başlayacak. Etkinlik öncesinde ise saat 20.00’de Cem Mansur’un katılımıyla “Cem Mansur ile Konser Üzerine” başlıklı bir söyleşi gerçekleştirilecek.
Gecenin programı Maurice Ravel’in Ölü Bir Prenses için Pavan adlı eseriyle başlayacak. Ardından Cem Önertürk’ün solistliğinde Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart’ın Re Majör Flüt Konçertosu seslendirilecek. Konserin devamında Claude Debussy’nin Küçük Süit adlı eseri ve Cem Güven’in Gedik Filarmoni Orkestrası için bestelediği Mavi dinleyiciyle buluşacak.
Konserin dikkat çeken bölümlerinden biri, genç besteci Cem Güven’in Mavi adlı eserinin ilk kez seslendirilecek olması. Besteci, eserini “hava seslerinden büyük armonilere bir yolculuk” olarak tanımlıyor. Orkestra için hazırlanan eser, çağdaş müzik repertuvarına yeni bir çalışma kazandıracak.
Mozart’ın Re Majör Flüt Konçertosu ise flütün teknik ve melodik olanaklarını ortaya koyan önemli eserler arasında yer alıyor. Ravel’in düşsel atmosferiyle öne çıkan Ölü Bir Prenses için Pavanı ve Debussy’nin piyano için besteledikten sonra orkestraya uyarlanan Küçük Süiti, gecenin programındaki diğer eserleri oluşturuyor.

Beşiktaş , UEFA Avrupa Ligi'nde Gürcistan'ın Batum kentinde İsrail ekibi Hapoel Beer-Sheva'yı 2-1 mağlup etti. Tribünlerde yaşanan olaylar ve maç sonundaki Filistin'e destek görüntüleri geceye damgasını vurdu. TFF Başkanı İbrahim Hacıosmanoğlu da CNN Türk canlı yayınına bağlanarak İsrail takımları, UEFA ile temasları ve olası cezalar hakkında konuştu.
Siyah beyazlıların olayların gölgesinde geçen gecede aldığı sonuç, TFF cephesinde de karşılık buldu. CNN Türk yayınında Beşiktaş camiasına destek veren Hacıosmanoğlu, tribündeki taraftarlar ve sahadaki oyuncular için şu ifadeleri kullandı:
'Beşiktaş taraftarına geçmiş olsun. Galibiyet için Beşiktaş futbolcularının gözlerinden öpüyorum. İyi bir ders verdiler.'
Batum'da yaşananların ardından UEFA ve güvenlik yetkilileriyle konuşan TFF Başkanı, girişimlerin sürdüğünü belirtti. Avrupa futbolundaki dengelere ve İsrail federasyonuna da değinen Hacıosmanoğlu şu açıklamayı yaptı:
'UEFA ve polis yetkilileriyle görüştüm. 55 tane federasyon var, sadece İsrail'in federasyon başkanı ile görüşmedim. Onların bir lobisi yok orada. Yönetimde birinin olması önemli değil, biz istediğimizi yaptırıyoruz. Girişimlerimiz devam ediyor. Beşiktaş taraftarını tebrik ederim.'
İsrail takımlarının Türkiye'de maç yapmasına karşı olduğunu açıkça dile getiren Hacıosmanoğlu, İsrail'in futboldan men edilmesi gerektiğini UEFA toplantılarında savunduğunu anlatırken şu sözleri kullandı:
'İsrail bebek katili, UEFA toplantılarında söyledim. Bunların futboldan atılması gerektiğini de çok kez dile getirdim. Bir önce Beşiktaş maçına, İsrail takımı ile oynadıkları, kafile ile gitmiştim. Bir devlet politikamız var, İsrail takımlarını Türkiye'ye biz istemiyoruz.'
TFF Başkanı, Beşiktaş'ın karşılaşmayı İstanbul 'da oynamak istemesi ihtimali için de şu değerlendirmeyi yaptı:
'Beşiktaş, İstanbul'da oynamak isteseydi, UEFA buna izin verirdi. İsrail takımı gelmezse, hükmen mağlup olurdu. UEFA güvenlik gerekçesiyle maçı başka bir ülkede oynatmak gibi gaflete düşmez. Zaten başkan dostumuz, Türkiye'ye karşı böyle bir şey içerisinde olamazlar.'
Hacıosmanoğlu, Türkiye'nin güvenliği sağlayabileceğini vurgulayıp sözlerini şöyle sürdürdü:
'Bebek katili bir ülkenin takımı bu topraklarda oynayamaz! UEFA sadece güvenlik ister. Bizim devletimiz güvenliği sağlar, İstanbul'da maç oynanırdı ama biz bu ülke topraklarına gelmelerini istemiyoruz.'
Bitiş düdüğünden sonra Beşiktaşlı futbolcular Filistin'e destek pankartının önünde fotoğraf çektirdi, Ouattara da Filistin bayrağını UEFA yazısının üzerine astı. Bu görüntüler olası bir yaptırım ihtimalini akıllara getirdi. Tribünlerdeki olaylar ile bayrak konusunu birbirinden ayıran Hacıosmanoğlu, ceza sorusuna şu yanıtı verdi:
'Taşkınlıklardan ufak cezalar olabilir. Ancak Filistin bayrağı nedeniyle ceza gelmesi söz konusu değil.'

Beşiktaş ile İsrail takımı Hapoel Beer-Sheva arasında Batum'da oynanan UEFA Avrupa Ligi maçı, tribünlerdeki gerginlik nedeniyle yarım kalan bir geceye dönüştü. Filistin bayrağı açan taraftarlara Gürcü polisi saldırdı. Olaylar yalnızca Türkiye'de değil, İsrail basınında da geniş yer buldu. Gürcistan'da gözaltına alınan 16 taraftar serbest bırakıldı. Peki, İsrail basını Beşiktaş maçını nasıl gördü?
Karşılaşma öncesinde Batum sokaklarında yaşananlar, İsrail spor medyasının gündemine ilk sırada girdi. Sport5, Beşiktaş taraftarlarının kentte Filistin'e destek yürüyüşü yaptığını, Filistin bayrakları taşıdığını ve özgürlük çağrısı içeren pankartlar açtığını yazdı. Haberde bu gösterilerin Hapoel Beer-Sheva taraftarları açısından güvenlik endişesi doğurduğuna da dikkat çekildi.
Ynet, Batum merkezinde toplanan yüzlerce Türk taraftarın Filistin ve Türkiye bayraklarıyla yürüdüğünü aktardı. Walla Sport ise daha sert bir dil kullandı; İsrail karşıtı sloganlara yer verirken Fenerbahçe ve Trabzonspor taraftarlarından bazılarının da gösterilere katıldığı iddiasını haberine taşıdı. Ortak nokta belliydi: Maçın futbol boyutu ikinci plana itilmiş, siyasi atmosfer öne çıkarılmıştı.
Israel Hayom, tribündeki ilk gerginliği 'provokasyon' çerçevesinde verdi. Habere göre bir Beşiktaş taraftarı Filistin bayrağını Hapoel Beer-Sheva taraftarlarının bulunduğu bölüme doğru açtı, güvenlik görevlileri müdahale etti ve bu sırada taraftarlarla görevliler arasında gerginlik yaşandı. Gazete ayrıca İsrailli taraftarların güvenlik kaygılarını ve maçın İstanbul yerine Gürcistan'da oynanmasının arka planını öne çıkardı.
Sport5 ise Gürcistan polisinin Filistin bayrağı açan Beşiktaş taraftarlarına müdahalesini ve ardından yaşanan arbedeyi haberleştirdi. Haberde yaklaşık 10 taraftarın gözaltına alındığı ileri sürüldü. Ancak gözaltı sayısına ve güvenlik görevlilerine atfedilen ifadelere dair bağımsız bir resmi açıklama bulunmuyor; bu bilgiler Sport5'in aktardığı iddialar olarak yer aldı.
Maç, 25-26. dakikalarda kritik bir noktaya geldi. Müdahale ve arbedenin ardından hakem ve futbolcular güvenlik gerekçesiyle soyunma odasına yöneldi. Uluslararası basında polis müdahalesi sırasında biber gazı kullanıldığı yazıldı; İspanyol AS gazetesi ise karşılaşmanın yarım saat dolmadan askıya alındığını duyurdu.
İncelenen haberler üç eksende toplanıyor: Hapoel Beer-Sheva taraftarlarının güvenliği ve maç öncesi tedbirler, Beşiktaş taraftarlarının taşıdığı bayraklar, açtığı pankartlar ve attığı sloganlar, bir de Gürcü güvenlik güçlerinin müdahalesiyle maçın durması.
Kullanılan dil ise aynı değil. Bazı yayınlar Beşiktaş taraftarlarının davranışını provokasyon olarak tanımlarken, bazıları Filistin gösterilerini ve polis müdahalesini daha mesafeli bir üslupla aktardı.
Yaklaşık 40 dakikalık aranın ardından devam eden maçı Beşiktaş 2-1 kazandı.
'Eşi benzeri görülmemiş kaos: Beşiktaş ile Hapoel Beer Sheva arasındaki maçın durmasına neden olan kargaşa'
'Türk futbol kulübü Beşiktaş ile İsrail'in Hapoel Beerşeba takımı arasındaki UEFA Avrupa Ligi maçı, Türk taraftarların ayaklanıp Gürcistan güvenlik güçleriyle çatışması üzerine geçici olarak durduruldu.'

Türkiye Futbol Federasyonu (TFF) Başkanı İbrahim Hacıosmanoğlu, İsrail ile Türk takımları arasındaki iç saha Avrupa maçlarının Türkiye istemediği için yurt dışında oynandığını söyledi.
Avrupa Ligi’nde Beşiktaş’ın iç saha maçı olarak fikstürde yer alan Hapoel Beer Sheva karşılaşması Türk makamlarının UEFA’ya ‘güvenlik gerekçesiyle’ İstanbul’da oynanamayacağını bildirmesi üzerine Gürcistan’a taşınmıştı.
Dün (26 Kasım) Batum’da oynanan maçın seremonisinde Beşiktaşlı futbolcular Hapoel Beer Sheva’lı futbolcularla tokalaşmadı. Maçın 25’inci dakikasında ‘Filistin’e Özgürlük’ pankartlarının açıldığı tribünde çıkan olaylar Danimarkalı hakem Morten Krogh maçı durdurdu . Gürcistan polisi tribündeki Beşiktaş taraftarına biber gazı sıktı, stada takviye çevik kuvvet de getirildi.
Ancak 35 dakika sonra yeniden başlayabilen maçı, Beşiktaş 2-1 kazandı.
CNN Türk yayını na telefonla bağlanan Hacıosmanoğlu, İsrail ile Türk takımları arasındaki Avrupa maçlarının yurt dışında oynanmasını ‘devlet politikası’ diye açıkladı.
TFF’nin UEFA’da en güçlü dönemini yaşadığını öne süren federasyon başkanı “İstediğimizi yaptırıyoruz” dedi. Hatta 2027’deki UEFA Başkanlığı seçimlerine atfen “Birini koyarız oraya” iddiasında bulundu:
“Öncelikle Beşiktaş taraftarına geçmiş olsun, diyorum. Galibiyet için de Beşiktaş oyuncularının gözlerinden öpüyorum ve camiayı tebrik ediyorum. İyi bir ders verdiler, bütün bu kargaşadan sonra.
Elbette ki UEFA ve polis yetkilileriyle görüştüm. Hatta 30 dakikaya yakın bir ara oldu. Tatil edilmesi konusunda da en üst düzeyde görüşmelerim oldu. 55 tane federasyonu var, UEFA’nın. Tek görüşmediğim İsrail’in federasyon başkanıdır. (UEFA Başkanı Aleksander) Ceferin iyi bir dostum, onu bile araya koydu ama görüşmedim. Onların öyle bir lobisi yok orada. Türkiye Futbol Federasyonu, tarihinde UEFA’da en güçlü olduğu dönemi yaşıyor. Ne istiyorsak, istediğimizi yaptırıyoruz. Zaten nisanda seçim var, birini koyarız oraya (UEFA Başkanlığı seçimlerini kastediyor) .
Bu olaylarla ilgili de elbette resmi açıklamamızı da yaptık. UEFA’da girişimlerimiz devam ediyor. Tasvip etmiyoruz futbolda bunları. Bırakın sadece burada konuşmayı, UEFA toplantılarında da bütün konuşmalarımda da söylerken çok ağır cümleler kullanarak, bebek katilleri olarak söylüyorum. Hatta UEFA toplantısında ‘Ukrayna-Rusya savaşıyor, Rusya tamamen men edildi ama burada bebek katilleri hala futbol camiasının içinde, bunları da atmamız gerek’ diye defalarca söyledim. Girişimlerimiz o konuda var.
Şunun da bilinmesini istiyorum: Bir önceki Beşiktaş maçına ben de kafileyle beraber gitmiştim. Biliyorsunuz yine İsrail takımıyla oynuyordu. Burada bizim bir devlet politikamız var, İsrail takımlarını Türkiye’ye istemiyoruz. UEFA ‘Beşiktaş’a gideceksin Gürcistan’da veyahut Macaristan’da oynayacaksın’ demiyor. Biz onları Türkiye’ye istemiyoruz. Yoksa ‘Biz Beşiktaş İnönü Stadı’nda oynayacak maçını’ deseydik, UEFA İstanbul’da oynatırdı. İsrail takımı gelmezse hükmen mağlup olurdu.”

The Forest Service’s work will ‘help normalize’ talk happening ‘for decades’, says ‘wood ape’ conservancy director
When the Forest Service, one of the US government’s less sexy departments, quietly posted three documents to its website in mid-October, it was probably hoping to avoid a fuss.
It didn’t succeed. The files were about Bigfoot, after all, and their publication sparked interest from around the globe, with Bigfoot enthusiasts hopeful that this could be a key step step in the road to proving the creature is real.
“It’s going to help normalize the conversation that the people in this community have been having for decades,” said Tami Grimes. She’s a director at the North American Wood Ape Conservancy (Nawac), which investigates sightings of Bigfoot (the organization prefers the term ‘wood ape’, as it is less mythical-sounding). Nawac collects reports and, if Bigfoot encounters are deemed legitimate, sends out volunteers to gather, or attempt to gather, evidence.
“The release of these papers shows that there have been government reports done to document it. It shows that there was enough to the incidents that the Forest Service took the incidents seriously.”
Grimes, 59, has reason to be invested. She said she has seen Bigfoot several times – the first when she was four-years-old. Her family lived close to Green Swamp, in central Florida, and Grimes recalls looking out of the bedroom one night and seeing a bipedal creature, covered in dark brown-to-back colored hair, staring back at her. It was 7ft tall, and powerfully built.
“The best way to describe the physique is that it was like Lou Ferrigno,” Grimes said, referring to the bodybuilder-turned-actor who was crowned Mr Universe in 1974 and later played the Hulk in the CBS TV show The Incredible Hulk. “It was broad across the shoulders, incredibly muscular,” she said.
The creature, which Grimes believes was a Bigfoot, was not impeded by its bulky frame. It ran off at a “rapid speed”, Grimes recalls. She had nightmares for 25 years after the event. She then had another run-in with a Bigfoot in December 2003, when she and a friend went looking for one in a swamp in Florida. She saw a figure standing in the woods, swaying from side to side. It turned to look at her, Grimes said, then it tried and failed to hide behind a pine tree: “Its face and its backside was still sticking out from behind the tree,” before running off into the woods.
Grimes had been watching the figure through a thermal camera, but unfortunately she had only recently purchased the camera and did not know how to press record, so no footage was captured.
Bigfoot, or Sasquatch, has captured American imaginations for decades. Believers say the creature inhabits forests in the US and Canada, being particularly common in the Pacific north-west. Commonly described as tall, strong-looking and foul-smelling, there have been thousands of reports of sightings submitted to amateur Bigfoot tracking organizations like Nawac and the Bigfoot field researchers organization.
Yet Bigfoot is considered by many to be a myth, its alleged existence attributable to folk tales and whimsy, and governmental discussion of it is rare. The White House, the US Department of Defense and the US Department of the Interior all declined to comment on Bigfoot to the Guardian.
The Forest Service did reply. In a statement, a spokesman said: “Stories of Bigfoot, Sasquatch, and other legendary beings have long been part of the cultural fabric of many regions, reflecting a rich tradition of folklore, oral history, and storytelling that surrounds our public lands. While the Forest Service does not endorse or make any claims regarding the existence of such creatures, we appreciate the public’s enthusiasm for exploring and learning about our public lands.”
Other sources were more forthright. A chatbot on the National Park Service website said there “is no scientific evidence that Bigfoot exists as a real animal”, while Encyclopedia Britannica said “most scientists do not recognize the creature’s existence”. Bigfoot does not feature in the National Wildlife Federation’s database of fauna found in the US.
The amount of Bigfoot hoaxes likely hasn’t helped boost its credibility. In one case, two men said they found a Bigfoot body, but when they handed it over to researchers it turned out to be a rubber gorilla suit. A 2014 study of 30 hair samples alleged to be yeti or Bigfoot found that all the hair was from extant species, including a black bear, a cow and a human.
Still, there was plenty of excitement when the forestry service quietly released those Bigfoot-related documents, even if the content was a little underwhelming. One of the files was merely a copy of a newspaper article, which reported that mysterious tracks had been discovered in Montana. Another was a 1980 essay written by someone called Leo Kinney , in which Kinney wrote that he and three others had encountered something in the woods: a creature “that walked on its hind legs that altho [sic] there wasn’t actual sightings, tracks, a strong odor and a gruntling sound were observed”.
The file that received the most attention was probably a report which had been commissioned by the US Department of Agriculture. In the report, Rodney Johnson, a wildlife biologist, said the USDA had asked him to accompany a group in the Umatilla national forest, in Portland, to investigate a reported finding of Bigfoot tracks – suggesting that at least someone at the department thought Bigfoot worthy of further study.
Johnson made plaster casts of four different foot or paw prints at two locations in the forest. He examined them, but found that the tracks “were made by something other than a 300 pound plus two-footed being” – aka, not Bigfoot. Johnson listed eight reasons for his conclusion, finding that the tracks did not extend deeply into the mud, that the stride length did not change even when they tracked uphill, that “forest litter”, like leaves, had been brushed aside prior to making the track, and that the tracks came to an abrupt end in the forest.
Some Bigfoot theories, however, account for that last point.
“It sounds more and more like alien or extraterrestrial than it does animal,” said Ronny LeBlanc, who starred in the Travel Channel show Expedition Bigfoot, which saw him and other experts search for Bigfoot at various locations. LeBlanc believes Bigfoot, or the creature known as Bigfoot, may be inter-dimensional or may use telepathy – or both – to evade capture.
“We’re hearing about UFOs coming in and out of the water. We’re hearing about underwater bases and all this stuff,” LeBlanc said, echoing claims made by UFO-curious Republican congressman Tim Burchett. Burchett, who has been a lead figure in demanding the government release information pertaining to UFOs, said last year that an admiral had told him about large unidentified craft “moving at hundreds of miles an hour underwater”.
“So for me, it’s not that far of a stretch that you have something running around in the forest,” LeBlanc said.
He has had his own Bigfoot experiences. He said he and another man once encountered an “orange orb” in a forest, which “split into two eyes” before taking on the shape of an 8ft tall Bigfoot. “We were with a clairvoyant medium, so I don’t know if that had something to do with it,” LeBlanc said.
He compared the relatively low lack of sightings of Bigfoot to the case of air force pilots who were reluctant to tell their commanding officers that they had seen UFOs. Several finally came forward and shared their experiences with the 60 Minutes news show in 2021, sparking an increased interest in a taboo subject, and prompting several congressional hearings.
“In that same vein, you have people [asking]: “How come hunters don’t see [Bigfoot]? or ‘How come loggers don’t see them?’
“They do. They’re just not talking about it,” he said. “Forestry workers are finding nests in tracks and having sightings, and they’re afraid to kind of pas…

Kitap dünyasına açılan kapınızı aralayın! En sevdiğiniz kitapları indirimli fiyatlarla keşfedin ve hayal gücünüzü genişletin.
Türkiye Musiki Eseri Sahipleri Meslek Birliği (MESAM) 1986 yılında başlayan 40 yıllık hak ve telif mücadelesini gala gecesiyle kutladı. İstanbul Lütfi Kırdar Kongre Merkezi Rumeli Salonu’nda düzenlenen MESAM 40’ıncı Yıl Gala Programı ve Ödül Töreni, müzik sektörünün dünü ile bugününü buluşturdu.
MESAM’ın 40 yıllık köklü yolculuğunu anlatan özel tanıtım filmiyle başlayan gece, KARAF Konseri ile müzik ziyafetine dönüştü. Yemekli gala programında Arabeskten Rap’e, Pop’tan Rock’a, halk müziğinden Türk sanat müziğine kadar müziğin her rengi ve her kuşağı tek bir çatı altında buluştu.
Gecenin açılış konuşmasını yapan MESAM Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Recep Ergül, kurumun 40 yıllık fikri mülkiyet mücadelesinin uluslararası arenadaki büyük başarısına dikkat çekti. Ergül, konuşmasında şu ifadelere yer verdi:
"Türkiye’nin ilk ve en büyük müzik meslek birliği olan MESAM bugün 40 yaşında. Kırk yıldır bu topraklarda fikri mülkiyet ve eser sahipleri adına kararlı bir mücadele yürütüyoruz. MESAM’ın ortaya koyduğu vizyoner çalışmalar, ülkemizin Uluslararası Yazar ve Besteciler Konfederasyonu (CISAC) verilerinde son sıralardan kurtularak 32’nci sıraya kadar yükselmesini sağladı. 40’ıncı yılımız anısına gerçekleştirdiğimiz bu görkemli tören, sanatın birleştirici gücünün toplumumuza en güçlü yansımasıdır. Bugün burada, farklı kuşakların ve farklı müzik türlerinin kucaklaştığı eşsiz bir Türkiye mozaiğinin buluşmasına tanıklık ediyoruz."
MESAM 40’ıncı Yıl Ödülleri’nde değerlendirmeler yalnızca başarı, sanatsal üretim, eserlerin kalıcılığı ve sektöre verilen emek temelinde yapıldı. Gecede; büyük yapım şirketleriyle çalışan sanatçılar da bağımsız müzisyenler de aynı hakkaniyet anlayışıyla onurlandırıldı.
Zeki Müren, Mahzuni Şerif, Yıldırım Gürses, Yusuf Hayaloğlu ve Atilla Özdemiroğlu gibi müzik tarihimize silinmez izler bırakan ustalar saygıyla anılırken; ödülleri aileleri ve yasal temsilcileri tarafından alkışlar eşliğinde teslim alındı. Gecede Fazıl Say ve Hakkı Bulut gibi dev isimlerin yanı sıra Semicenk, Mabel Matiz, Gazapizm, Burak Bulut ve Sagopa Kajmer gibi günümüzün öne çıkan sanatçıları da ödüllerine kavuştu.
Gecede üç ana kategoride toplam 35 ödül takdim edildi. Güncel üretimi ve yüksek etkiyi simgeleyen 18 Başarı Ödülü, Türk müziğine adanmış ömür boyu katkıyı onurlandıran 13 Onur Ödülü ve MESAM’ın kurumsal çalışmalarına destek veren kurum ve isimlere sunulan 4 Teşekkür Ödülü sahiplerini buldu.

Karadağ'ın Türk vatandaşlarına vize zorunluluğu getirmesinin ardından Ankara 'dan benzer bir adım geldi. Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan 'ın imzasını taşıyan karar Resmi Gazete 'de yayımlandı. Düzenleme, iki ülke arasında 2008 yılında imzalanan vize muafiyeti anlaşmasını yakından ilgilendiriyor.
26 Kasım 2026 tarihli ve Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan imzalı karar, 27 Kasım tarihli Resmi Gazete 'de yayımlandı. Düzenlemeyle Karadağ vatandaşlarının Türkiye'ye vizesiz giriş yapmasına imkan tanıyan uygulama durduruldu. Ankara 'nın bu adımı, Karadağ'ın Türk vatandaşlarına vize zorunluluğu getirmesinin ardından geldi.
Durdurma kararı, Karadağ'ın umuma mahsus yani bordo pasaport taşıyan vatandaşlarını ilgilendiriyor. 18 Ocak 2008'de imzalanan anlaşmaya ilişkin Resmi Gazete 'deki metinde şu ifadeler yer aldı:
'18/1/2008 tarihinde imzalanan ve 3/3/2008 tarihli ve 2008/13335 sayılı Bakanlar Kurulu Kararıyla onaylanan 'Türkiye Cumhuriyeti Hükümeti ile Karadağ Hükümeti Arasında Karşılıklı Vize Muafiyeti Anlaşması' hükümlerinin Karadağ'ın umuma mahsus pasaport hamili vatandaşları bakımından uygulanmasının durdurulmasına, 9 sayılı Cumhurbaşkanlığı Kararnamesinin 3 üncü maddesi gereğince karar verilmiştir.'
Türkiye ile Karadağ arasında geçen yıl yaşanan diplomatik krizin ardından Karadağ hükümeti, Türk vatandaşlarına tanıdığı vizesiz seyahat uygulamasını sona erdirerek vize zorunluluğu getirmişti. Karar 1 Kasım'da yürürlüğe girmişti. Bu tarihten önce Türk vatandaşları Karadağ'da 30 güne kadar vizesiz kalabiliyordu. Avrupa Birliği vize politikalarına uyum kapsamında Türkiye'nin yanı sıra Rusya , Belarus, Çin ve Suudi Arabistan vatandaşlarının muafiyeti de aynı tarihte sona ermişti.

Şebnem Bozoklu , 1 Aralık Salı akşamı ekran yolculuğuna başlayacak dizide Döne karakterine hayat veriyor. Hayranlarının karşısına bambaşka bir rolle çıkmaya hazırlanan oyuncu, Döne’yi artık kendisine çok yakın hissettiğini söyledi:
“Daha önce oynamadığım özelliklere sahip bir karakter Döne. İlk karşılaştığımda benim için bir yabancıydı. Şimdi ise canımdan da yakın hissediyorum onu. Tanıdıkça karşıma çok derinlikli ve özel bir kadın çıktı. Birlikte müthiş bir maceraya çıktık.”
Oyuncu, bir dönem işinde yer almanın keyfini yaşadığını açıkladı. Bozoklu, “Dizimizin geçtiği coğrafya, dönem, insan ilişkileri ve yarattığı gerçeklik hissinin seyirciyi sarıp sarmalayacağını düşünüyorum” dedi.

Kanal D’nin merakla beklenen dizisi Susuz Yaz’da Yeter rolüyle izleyici karşısına çıkmaya hazırlanan İrem Sak, heyecanını anlattı. 1 Aralık Salı akşamı ekran yolculuğuna başlayacak proje ile kariyerinde bir ilki yaşayacak olan oyuncu, “İlk dönem işim. Her zaman hayatımda böyle bir deneyimin olmasını istedim. Çok heyecanlıyım” diye konuştu.
Adana’da çekilen Susuz Yaz’da seyirciyi gerçekçi ve etkileyici bir atmosferin beklediğini belirten Sak, “Setimiz, köylerimiz, evlerimiz çok güzel” diyerek sözlerini şöyle sürdürdü: Ben her geldiğimde çok mutlu oluyorum. Onlar da izlerken bence çok mutlu olacaklar.
Motivasyonunun üst seviyede olduğunu ifade eden İrem Sak, “İstanbul’u, evimizi, sevdiklerimizi ve düzenimizi bırakıp buraya, Adana’ya gelmek gerçekten biraz motivasyon isteyen bir şey” dedikten sonra motivasyon kaynağını şöyle açıkladı: Beni her şeyden önce motive eden şey hikâye. Hikâyeye çok inanıyor ve ona çok motive oluyorum.
Seyircilerin diziyi izlerken karakterlerle güçlü bir bağ kuracağına dikkat çeken başarılı oyuncu, şunları söyledi: Seyircilerimiz izlerken de izledikten sonra da “Ben onun yaptığını yapar mıydım?” ya da “Bana yapılsa ne hissederdim, nasıl tepki verirdim?” dedirtirsek çok mutlu olurum. O gerçekçilikte bir iş olacağına inanıyorum. Hikâyemizin ele aldığı konular buna çok müsait.
Susuz Yaz’ın hikâyesinde önemli bir yere sahip olan Yeter; çalışkan, sabırlı ve güçlü sezgilere sahip bir kadın. Ailesini ve evliliğini korumak için her türlü fedakârlığı yapabilecek cesarette. Sakin ve uyumlu görünümünün ardında ise haksızlık karşısında mücadele etmekten çekinmeyen, gerektiğinde stratejik hamleler yapabilen güçlü bir karakter yatıyor.

Dizinin hikâyesi, Adana’nın Çarlak köyünde geçiyor. Osman’ın (Mert Ramazan Demir) Bahar’a duyduğu büyük aşk, iki kardeş arasındaki dengeleri değiştiriyor. Sevdiği kadınla yeni bir hayat kurmaya çalışan Osman’ın karşısına Hasan’ın (Batuhan Bozkurt Yüzgüleç) gizli planları çıkıyor. Köyde su ve toprak paylaşımı nedeniyle büyüyen anlaşmazlıklar ise zamanla iki kardeşin hayatını geri dönülmez şekilde değiştirecek olaylara dönüşüyor.

Gedik Filarmoni Orkestrası, 16 Aralık'ta şef Cem Mansur yönetiminde ve flüt sanatçısı Cem Önertürk'ün solistliğinde müzikseverlere klasik müziğin farklı dönemlerinden eserleri bir araya getiren bir konser sunacak.
Konser öncesinde saat 20.00'de Cem Mansur'un katılımıyla Cem Mansur ile Konser Üzerine başlıklı söyleşi gerçekleştirilecek. Saat 20.30'da başlayacak konserde Maurice Ravel'in "Ölü Bir Prenses için Pavan", Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart'ın "Re Majör Flüt Konçertosu", Claude Debussy'nin "Küçük Süit" ve genç besteci Cem Güven'in "Mavi" adlı eseri seslendirilecek.
Programda yer alan Mozart'ın "Re Majör Flüt Konçertosu", bestecinin flüt için kaleme aldığı iki konçertodan biri olarak dikkati çekiyor. Melodik zenginliği ve zarif anlatımıyla öne çıkan eser, flüt sanatçısı Cem Önertürk'ün yorumuyla dinleyiciyle buluşacak.
Konserin öne çıkan bölümlerinden biri de genç besteci Cem Güven'in Gedik Filarmoni Orkestrası için bestelediği Mavi adlı eserinin ilk seslendirilişi olacak.
Güven'in "hava seslerinden büyük armonilere bir yolculuk" olarak tanımladığı eser, çağdaş müziğin anlatım olanaklarını orkestral bir yorumla dinleyiciye sunacak. Konserde Fransız besteciler Maurice Ravel ve Claude Debussy'nin eserleri de yer alacak.
Ravel'in Velazquez'in bir tablosundan esinlenerek bestelediği "Ölü Bir Prenses için Pavan", programda yer alırken Debussy'nin başlangıçta piyano için bestelediği, daha sonra orkestra için düzenlenen dört bölümlük Küçük Süit'i de seslendirilecek.

Türkiye Musiki Eseri Sahipleri Meslek Birliği (MESAM), 1986 yılında başlayan 40 yıllık hak ve telif mücadelesini gala gecesiyle kutladı. İstanbul Lütfi Kırdar Kongre Merkezi Rumeli Salonu’nda düzenlenen MESAM 40’ıncı Yıl Gala Programı ve Ödül Töreni , müzik sektörünün dünü ile bugününü buluşturdu.
MESAM’ın 40 yıllık köklü yolculuğunu anlatan özel tanıtım filmiyle başlayan gece, KARAF Konseri ile müzik ziyafetine dönüştü. Yemekli gala programında Arabeskten Rap’e, Pop’tan Rock’a, halk müziğinden Türk sanat müziğine kadar müziğin her rengi ve her kuşağı tek bir çatı altında buluştu.
Gecenin açılış konuşmasını yapan MESAM Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Recep Ergül, kurumun 40 yıllık fikri mülkiyet mücadelesinin uluslararası arenadaki büyük başarısına dikkat çekti. Ergül, konuşmasında şu ifadelere yer verdi:
"Türkiye’nin ilk ve en büyük müzik meslek birliği olan MESAM bugün 40 yaşında. Kırk yıldır bu topraklarda fikri mülkiyet ve eser sahipleri adına kararlı bir mücadele yürütüyoruz. MESAM’ın ortaya koyduğu vizyoner çalışmalar, ülkemizin Uluslararası Yazar ve Besteciler Konfederasyonu (CISAC) verilerinde son sıralardan kurtularak 32’nci sıraya kadar yükselmesini sağladı. 40’ıncı yılımız anısına gerçekleştirdiğimiz bu görkemli tören, sanatın birleştirici gücünün toplumumuza en güçlü yansımasıdır. Bugün burada, farklı kuşakların ve farklı müzik türlerinin kucaklaştığı eşsiz bir Türkiye mozaiğinin buluşmasına tanıklık ediyoruz."

MasterChef 'in 26 Kasım akşamı yayınlanan yeni bölümünde Muhammed'in kaptan olduğu mavi takım ile Eyyüp Can'ın kaptan olduğu kırmızı takım bir kez daha karşı karşıya geldi. Haftanın ikinci dokunulmazlık oyununda takımlar, 7 çeşit Fransız yemeği hazırladı.
Hazırlık sürecinde mavi takımda Nice Salatası'nı hazırlayan Ayşe'ye sos konusunda Tolğa yardımcı oldu. Ancak hazırlanan sosu yoğun ve tat olarak keskin bulan Ayşe zeytinyağı ile açarak müdahale etti.
Tadım sırasında da Ayşe'nin sosu Tolğa ve Nilay'ın hazırladığını söylemesi üzerine Tolğa olanları şeflere anlattı. Şefler de kazanan tarafın kırmızı takım olduğunu, mavi takımın sosunun kıvamını çok akışkan bulduklarını, sebzelere bile yapışmadığını söyledi.
Tadım sonrası oyunu kazanan taraf kırmızı takım oldu. Şefler, bireysel dokunulmazlık için stüdyoya gelen mavi takımla salatayı konuştu.
Söz alan Ayşe, "Bu salata sosu meselesi daha sonuç açıklanmadan olay oldu. Tolğa beni kötülemeye başladı tuhaf bir şekilde" deyince Tolğa araya girdi.
Sinirlenen Tolğa, "Bunlarla tartışmak kadar kötü bir şey yok. Kendisine olması gerekeni söyledim ama kabul etmedi. Reçete kendisinin de ben de geri çekildim. Seni kötüleyecek bir tane cümlemi söyleyin ben buradan diskalifiye olmak istiyorum. Yeter. Ben bunlarla mı uğraşacağım şefim?" dedi.
Sonrasında sözünü bitiren Ayşe, sosun daha sıvı olması gerektiğini düşündüğünü tadını da beğenmeyince müdahale ettiğini belirtti ve "Daha yemeğin sonucu açıklanmadan ‘ben sosu çok güzel yaptım da senin yüzünden böyle oldu’ demek takım arkadaşına saygısızlık" dedi.
Bunun üzerine Tolğa, "Bence burada bir kadınla konuşmak tamamen saygısızlık. Merhaba demek bile MasterChef'te saygısızlık. Bence bunlar böyle. Kime bir şeyler söylersek bu onu algılıyor" deyince Somer Şef araya girdi.
Somer Sivrioğlu, "Yine de genelleme yapmayalım. Kadın olarak deme. Ayşe'yle öyle olabilir" dedi.
Tolğa da "Şefim ben burada hangi kadına bir şey söylesem ben saygısızmışım, kötülemişim. Öyle bir şey olmamasına rağmen oldu diyorlar. Ben bunlardan gerçekten bıktım, ben bunlarla uğraşmak istemiyorum şefim" dedi.
Somer Şef bunun üzerine "Tolğacığım konu Ayşe ya Ayşe hakkında yap. Kadınlar hakkında diye niye bir genelleme yapıyorsun?" dedi.
Tolğa'nın Somer Şef'e "Siz de önünü kesiyorsunuz" itirazıyla Somer Şef sinirlendi.
"Tolğacığım ben senin jürinim. İster sözünü keserim, ister dışarı atarım saygısızlık yapma. Sana bir laf söylüyorum. Ben burada seni korumaya çalışıyorum. Sana yardımcı olmak mı suç? Ne konuşursan konuş" diyerek stüdyoyu terk etti.
Somer Şef gittikten sonra Mehmet Şef hak verince Tolğa da "Hiç de haklı değil. Ben hepsinden aynı tepkiyi görüyorum şefim" dedi.
Bunun ardından Mehmet Yalçınkaya da "Diğer arkadaşlarınla da sorun yaşasan onlara bunları o gün söylersin. Bunu genelleme yapamayız, erkekler için de yapamayız. Ama Somer Şef dediğinde haklı ve gerçekten seni korumaya çalışıyor" ifadelerini kullandı.

Meghan Markle'ın pahalı Noel takvimi yapay zekâ ile yapılmış gibi görünüyor…
Haber başlıklarına göre çikolata dolu kutunun ön yüzünde, Sussex Dükü ve Düşesi'nin Montecito malikanesinin bir illüstrasyonu yer alıyor ve Daily Mail'in haberine göre bu illüstrasyon, "ChatGPT'nin yaratıcıları olan OpenAI tarafından yapılan" yapay zekâ araçları kullanılarak oluşturulmuş.
ABD'de 148 dolara, İngiltere'de ise 115 sterline satılan takvim, Markle'ın As Ever markasının bir parçası.
Markanın web sitesinde, "Ünlü Los Angeles çikolata üreticisi Compartes ile iş birliği içinde yaratılan bu sınırlı sayıda üretilen Noel takvimi, Meghan'ın Montecito'daki evinden ve bahçesinden ilham alan hatıra niteliğinde bir tasarımda 24 el yapımı çikolatayı ortaya çıkarıyor" ifadesi yer alıyor ve "Suits" dizisinin eski oyuncusunun ürünlerini hayranlıkla izlediği bir video da bulunuyor.
“Her özel çikolatanın içinde, Kaliforniya'nın taze ürünlerinden ve As Ever'ın favori lezzetlerinden, imza niteliğindeki sürülebilir kremalarımız da dahil olmak üzere, ilham alan tatlar bulunuyor ve Meghan'ın kişisel el yazısıyla yazılmış geri sayım numarasıyla tamamlanıyor.”
2025 yılında Markle, bir röportajda yapay zekadan korktuğunu itiraf etmiş ve kendisini "eski tarz" bir kız olarak tanımlamıştı.
Bu, Markle'ın markasının ilk kez eleştirilere maruz kalması değil.
El emeği ev eşyaları, süsler, organik meyvelerden yapılan reçeller, sabunlar, havlular gibi akla gelebilecek her türlü şeyin satıldığı şirketi As Ever ile hem başarılı bir iş kadını olarak anılmak isteyen hem de bu oluşumla lüks hayatlarını finanse edebilecek parayı kazanmaya çalışan Meghan Markle bu markayla ilgili daha önce de hem benzer hem de farklı sorunlar yaşamış ve deyim yerindeyse çok kereler topun ağzına konmuştu.
Geçen ay kraliyet yorumcuları, tatil koleksiyonundaki ürünlerin Buckingham Sarayı 2026 hediye sepeti koleksiyonundaki ürünlere çarpıcı bir benzerlik gösterdiğini fark etti.
As Ever'ın "Ev Sahibi Sepeti", nane ve limon-zencefil çayları, çeşitli meyve kremaları, çiçek serpiştirmeleri ve kokulu mumlar gibi lezzetlerle dolu. Sepetin fiyatı türüne göre değişiyor.
Buckingham Sarayı Noel Sepeti (192,50 $) tipik İngiliz lezzetleriyle dolu: Noel zencefilli çikolata barı, zencefilli mini kurabiyeler, bir chutney hediye seti, kıymalı turtalar, portakal-çikolatalı Noel bisküvileri, bir Noel pudingi ve 2026 Buckingham Sarayı resmi Noel süsü.
Markle, ekim ayında Instagram'da paylaştığı bir gönderide, çocukluğundan beri bir “girişimcilik ruhuna” sahip olduğunu; kendi saç tokalarını (scrunchie) yapıp sattığını, Girl Scout (İzci Kızlar) kurabiyeleri pazarladığını ve bir dondurulmuş yoğurt dükkanında çalıştığını anlattı.
Markle, " As Ever " markasının gösterdiği büyüme karşısında hayrete düştüğünü ifade ederek, tatil koleksiyonunu sunmaktan “büyük gurur ve minnettarlık” duyduğunu belirtti.
Bu, Markle, Prens Harry ve çocukları Prens Archie ile Prenses Lilibet’in 2018’den bu yana Birleşik Krallık’ta geçirecekleri ilk Noel olacak. Aile, 2019’daki tatil dönemini Kanada’da geçirmiş; Ocak 2020’de ise üst düzey kraliyet görevlerinden ayrıldıklarını duyurarak Los Angeles’a taşınmışlardı.

Athena, real name Karenjeet Kaur Bains, is among the Gladiators who will not be returning for the new series
Five Gladiators stars will not be returning to the BBC television show for its upcoming series, it is understood.
Athena, Comet, Bionic, Phantom and Cyclone will not be featured when the show returns in 2027.
A spokesperson for the production said the departing cast members "remain part of the wider Gladiators family" and are taking part in the ongoing arena tour, which comes to an end in December.
Gladiators relaunched on the BBC in 2024, having originally been aired on ITV from 1992 until 2000, and then on Sky between 2008 and 2009.
A spokesperson for Gladiators said: "We would like to thank our incredible Superhuman athletes for their contribution to the success and power of the Gladiators TV show.
"While they will not be appearing in Series 4, they remain part of the wider Gladiators family, and you can currently see them across the remaining shows in the UK Gladiator Arena Tour 2026."
Athena, real name Karenjeet Kaur Bains, 30, is a powerlifter and former track and field athlete, while Comet, real name, Ella-Mae Rayner, 31, is a former elite-level gymnast.
Bionic is the alter ego of 30-year-old body builder Matty Campbell, while Phantom is Toby Olubi, 39, who competed for Team GB in the bobsled at the 2018 Winter Olympics.
The upcoming series is due to introduce the first celebrity Gladiator, former England rugby union international and Celebrity Traitors star Joe Marler, who will use the name Mauler.
In June, the BBC said the series will return in 2027, hosted by father and son duo Bradley and Barney Walsh.
A celebrity special will also be broadcast over Christmas, featuring Big Brother presenter and I'm A Celebrity campmate AJ Odudu, TV presenter Chris Ramsey, social media star George Clarke and comedian Sara Pascoe.
